title: 05. Retrieval, Hybrid & Reranking: Reranking & Cross-encoders
summary: Covers The Two-Stage Retrieval Pipeline, Bi-Encoder vs Cross-Encoder, ColBERT — Late Interaction Reranking, VISUAL 11: Two-Stage Retrieval + Reranking.

sections.title: 13.1 The Two-Stage Retrieval Pipeline
sections.body:
```
STAGE 1: RETRIEVAL (Fast, Approximate)
══════════════════════════════════════
  BM25 + Vector Search → Top-100 candidates
  Speed: ~10-50ms
  Quality: Good

STAGE 2: RERANKING (Slow, Precise)
═══════════════════════════════════
  Cross-Encoder → Top-5 final results
  Speed: ~200-500ms (but only on 100 candidates)
  Quality: Excellent

Why two stages?
  Running Cross-Encoder on ALL documents = too slow ❌
  Running Cross-Encoder on Top-100 = fast enough ✅
```

sections.title: 13.2 Bi-Encoder vs Cross-Encoder
sections.body:
**What this code covers**

- Stage 1: Hybrid Search (BM25 + Vector) → Top-K candidates Stage 2: Cross-Encoder Reranking → Final Top-N
- Full two-stage retrieval pipeline
- Show before/after reranking comparison
- STAGE 1: Hybrid Retrieval
- STAGE 2: Cross-Encoder Reranking
- Score all pairs (cross-encoder processes jointly)
- Combine scores with candidates
- Re-sort by cross-encoder score

```
BI-ENCODER (Dense Retrieval):
  Query  → Encoder → Vector q
  Doc    → Encoder → Vector d
  Score  = cosine(q, d)
  
  ✅ Fast: vectors pre-computed
  ❌ No query-document interaction during encoding

CROSS-ENCODER (Reranking):
  [Query + Document] → Encoder → Relevance Score
  
  ✅ Full attention between query AND document
  ✅ Much more accurate
  ❌ Slow: must process each pair at query time
```

```python
from sentence_transformers import CrossEncoder
from typing import List, Tuple

class TwoStageRetriever:
    """
    Stage 1: Hybrid Search (BM25 + Vector) → Top-K candidates
    Stage 2: Cross-Encoder Reranking → Final Top-N
    """
    
    def __init__(self, 
                 hybrid_engine: HybridSearchEngine,
                 reranker_model: str = "cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2"):
        
        self.hybrid = hybrid_engine
        self.reranker = CrossEncoder(reranker_model)
        
        # Track performance
        self.metrics = {
            "stage1_latency": [],
            "stage2_latency": [],
            "candidates_before": [],
            "candidates_after": []
        }
    
    def retrieve(self, 
                  query: str,
                  stage1_k: int = 50,   # Retrieve 50 candidates
                  final_k: int = 5      # Return top 5 after reranking
                  ) -> List[dict]:
        """
        Full two-stage retrieval pipeline
        """
        import time
        
        # ── STAGE 1: Hybrid Retrieval ────────────────────────────────
        t1 = time.time()
        candidates = self.hybrid.search(query, top_k=stage1_k)
        stage1_time = time.time() - t1
        
        print(f"Stage 1: Retrieved {len(candidates)} candidates in {stage1_time*1000:.1f}ms")
        
        # ── STAGE 2: Cross-Encoder Reranking ─────────────────────────
        t2 = time.time()
        
        # Prepare query-document pairs
        pairs = [(query, c["text"]) for c in candidates]
        
        # Score all pairs (cross-encoder processes jointly)
        scores = self.reranker.predict(pairs, show_progress_bar=False)
        
        stage2_time = time.time() - t2
        print(f"Stage 2: Reranked {len(candidates)} docs in {stage2_time*1000:.1f}ms")
        
        # Combine scores with candidates
        for i, candidate in enumerate(candidates):
            candidate["rerank_score"] = float(scores[i])
            candidate["stage1_rank"] = candidate["rank"]
        
        # Re-sort by cross-encoder score
        reranked = sorted(candidates, key=lambda x: x["rerank_score"], reverse=True)
        
        # Add final rank and show rank changes
        for i, doc in enumerate(reranked[:final_k]):
            doc["final_rank"] = i + 1
            rank_change = doc["stage1_rank"] - doc["final_rank"]
            doc["rank_change"] = f"↑{rank_change}" if rank_change > 0 else f"↓{abs(rank_change)}" if rank_change < 0 else "═"
        
        return reranked[:final_k]
    
    def explain_reranking(self, query: str, top_k: int = 5):
        """Show before/after reranking comparison"""
        results = self.retrieve(query, stage1_k=20, final_k=top_k)
        
        print(f"\n{'='*70}")
        print(f"RERANKING RESULTS FOR: '{query}'")
        print(f"{'='*70}")
        print(f"{'Final':<6} {'Stage1':<7} {'Change':<8} {'Rerank Score':<15} Text")
        print(f"{'─'*70}")
        
        for doc in results:
            print(f"  {doc['final_rank']:<5} {doc['stage1_rank']:<7} "
                  f"{doc['rank_change']:<8} {doc['rerank_score']:<15.4f} "
                  f"{doc['text'][:50]}...")

# ─── DEMO OUTPUT ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Stage 1: Retrieved 20 candidates in 12.3ms
# Stage 2: Reranked 20 docs in 187.4ms
#
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# RERANKING RESULTS FOR: 'Python deep learning frameworks'
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Final  Stage1  Change   Rerank Score    Text
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#   1      3      ↑2      8.9234          PyTorch and TensorFlow are...
#   2      1      ↓1      7.4521          Python is excellent for ML...
#   3      7      ↑4      6.8834          Keras simplifies neural network...
#   4      2      ↓2      5.2341          Data science uses Python...
#   5      12     ↑7      4.9123          Deep learning requires GPU...
```

sections.title: 13.3 ColBERT — Late Interaction Reranking
sections.body:
```
ColBERT = Contextualized Late Interaction over BERT

Instead of ONE vector per doc, store vectors for EACH TOKEN.
Then compute MaxSim scores:

Score(q, d) = Σ  max  cos(qi, dj)
              qi  dj∈d

This captures fine-grained token-level interactions!
```

```python
class ColBERTScorer:
    """
    Simplified ColBERT late-interaction scoring.
    In production, use the official PLAID/ColBERT library.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, model_name: str = "bert-base-uncased"):
        from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModel
        self.tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
        self.model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(model_name)
        self.model.eval()
    
    def encode_tokens(self, text: str) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Get per-token contextual embeddings"""
        inputs = self.tokenizer(text, return_tensors="pt", 
                                 truncation=True, max_length=512)
        with torch.no_grad():
            outputs = self.model(**inputs)
        # Shape: (seq_len, hidden_size)
        token_embeddings = outputs.last_hidden_state.squeeze(0)
        # L2 normalize each token vector
        return torch.nn.functional.normalize(token_embeddings, p=2, dim=-1)
    
    def maxsim_score(self, query_vecs: torch.Tensor, 
                      doc_vecs: torch.Tensor) -> float:
        """
        MaxSim: for each query token, find max similarity to any doc token
        Score = sum of all query token maxsims
        """
        # (query_len, doc_len) cosine similarity matrix
        sim_matrix = torch.matmul(query_vecs, doc_vecs.T)
        
        # For each query token: max similarity over all doc tokens
        max_sims = sim_matrix.max(dim=1).values  # (query_len,)
        
        return max_sims.sum().item()
    
    def score(self, query: str, document: str) -> float:
        """Full ColBERT scoring"""
        q_vecs = self.encode_tokens(f"[Q] {query}")
        d_vecs = self.encode_tokens(f"[D] {document}")
        return self.maxsim_score(q_vecs, d_vecs)
```
